REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.body: Unless stated otherwise in this paragraph, equipment used for testing shall be calibrated before its initial use and at appropriate service intervals thereafter. An appropriate service interval shall be either equipment manufacturer recommendation or according to good engineering practice.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.1.title: Chassis dynamometer
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.1.body: The chassis dynamometer shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 2. to 2.4.2. inclusive of Annex B5.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.title: Evaporative emission measurement enclosure
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.body: The evaporative emission measurement enclosure shall be a gas-tight rectangular measuring chamber able to contain the vehicle under test. The vehicle shall be accessible from all sides and the enclosure when sealed shall be gas-tight in accordance with paragraph 4.2.3.3. of this annex. The inner surface of the enclosure shall be impermeable and non-reactive to hydrocarbons. The temperature conditioning system shall be capable of controlling the internal enclosure air temperature to follow the prescribed temperature versus time profile throughout the test, and an average tolerance of 1 °C over the duration of the test. The control system shall be tuned to provide a smooth temperature pattern that has a minimum of overshoot, hunting, and instability about the desired longterm ambient temperature profile. Interior surface temperatures shall not be less than 5 °C nor more than 55 °C at any time during the diurnal emission test. Wall design shall be such as to promote good dissipation of heat. Interior surface temperatures shall not be below 20 °C, nor above 52 °C for the duration of the hot soak rest. To accommodate the volume changes due to enclosure temperature changes, either a variable-volume or fixed-volume enclosure may be used.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.1.title: Variable-volume enclosure
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.1.body: The variable-volume enclosure expands and contracts in response to the temperature change of the air mass in the enclosure. Two potential means of accommodating the internal volume changes are movable panel(s), or a bellows design, in which an impermeable bag or bags inside the enclosure expand(s) and contracts(s) in response to internal pressure changes by exchanging air from outside the enclosure. Any design for volume accommodation shall maintain the integrity of the enclosure as specified in paragraph 4.2.3. of this annex over the specified temperature range. Any method of volume accommodation shall limit the differential between the enclosure internal pressure and the barometric pressure to a maximum value of •0.5 kPa. The enclosure shall be capable of latching to a fixed volume. A variable volume enclosure shall be capable of accommodating a +7 per cent change from its "nominal volume" (see paragraph 4.2.3.1.1. of this annex), taking into account temperature and barometric pressure variation during testing.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.2.title: Fixed-volume enclosure
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.2.body: The fixed-volume enclosure shall be constructed with rigid panels that maintain a fixed enclosure volume, and meet the requirements below.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.2.1.lb: 4.2.2.1. The enclosure shall be equipped with an outlet flow stream that withdraws air a…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.2.1.body: The enclosure shall be equipped with an outlet flow stream that withdraws air at a low, constant rate from the enclosure throughout the test. An inlet flow stream may provide make-up air to balance the outgoing flow with incoming ambient air. Inlet air shall be filtered with activated carbon to provide a relatively constant hydrocarbon level. Any method of volume accommodation shall maintain the differential between the enclosure internal pressure and the barometric pressure between 0 and -0.5 kPa.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.2.2.lb: 4.2.2.2. The equipment shall be capable of measuring the mass of hydrocarbon in the inle…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.2.2.body: The equipment shall be capable of measuring the mass of hydrocarbon in the inlet and outlet flow streams with a resolution of 0.01 gram. A bag sampling system may be used to collect a proportional sample of the air withdrawn from and admitted to the enclosure. Alternatively, the inlet and outlet flow streams may be continuously analysed using an on-line FID analyser and integrated with the flow measurements to provide a continuous record of the mass hydrocarbon removal.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.1.lb: 4.2.3.1. Initial determination of internal volume of the enclosure
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.1.title: Initial determination of internal volume of the enclosure

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.1.1.lb: 4.2.3.1.1. Before its initial use, the internal volume of the chamber shall be determined …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.1.1.body: Before its initial use, the internal volume of the chamber shall be determined as follows: The internal dimensions of the chamber are carefully measured, allowing for any irregularities such as bracing struts. The internal volume of the chamber is determined from these measurements. For variable-volume enclosures, the enclosure shall be latched to a fixed volume when the enclosure is held at an ambient temperature of 30 °C or at the choice of the manufacturer 29 °C. This nominal volume shall be repeatable within •0.5 per cent of the reported value.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.1.2.lb: 4.2.3.1.2. The net internal volume is determined by subtracting 1.42 m from the internal v…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.1.2.body: The net internal volume is determined by subtracting 1.42 m from the internal volume of the chamber. Alternatively the volume of the test vehicle with the luggage compartment and windows open may be used instead of the 1.42 m .

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.1.3.lb: 4.2.3.1.3. The chamber shall be checked as in paragraph 4.2.3.3. of this annex. If the pro…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.1.3.body: The chamber shall be checked as in paragraph 4.2.3.3. of this annex. If the propane mass does not correspond to the injected mass to within •2 per cent, then corrective action is required.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.title: Determination of chamber background emissions
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.body: This operation determines that the chamber does not contain any materials that emit significant amounts of hydrocarbons. The check shall be carried out at the enclosure's introduction to service, after any operations in the enclosure which may affect background emissions and at a frequency of at least once per year.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.1.lb: 4.2.3.2.1. Variable-volume enclosures may be operated in either latched or unlatched volum…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.1.body: Variable-volume enclosures may be operated in either latched or unlatched volume configuration, as described in paragraph 4.2.3.1.1. of this annex, ambient temperatures shall be maintained at 35 °C • 2 °C, or at the choice of the manufacturer 36 °C • 2 °C, throughout the 4-hour period mentioned below.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.2.lb: 4.2.3.2.2. Fixed volume enclosures shall be operated with the inlet and outlet flow stream…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.2.body: Fixed volume enclosures shall be operated with the inlet and outlet flow streams closed. Ambient temperatures shall be maintained at 35 °C • 2 °C, or at the choice of the manufacturer 36 °C • 2 °C, throughout the 4-hour period mentioned below.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.3.lb: 4.2.3.2.3. The enclosure may be sealed and the mixing fan operated for a period of up to 1…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.3.body: The enclosure may be sealed and the mixing fan operated for a period of up to 12 hours before the 4-hour background sampling period begins.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.4.lb: 4.2.3.2.4. The analyser (if required) shall be calibrated, then zeroed and spanned.
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.4.body: The analyser (if required) shall be calibrated, then zeroed and spanned.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.5.lb: 4.2.3.2.5. The enclosure shall be purged until a stable hydrocarbon reading is obtained, a…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.5.body: The enclosure shall be purged until a stable hydrocarbon reading is obtained, and the mixing fan turned on if not already on.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.6.lb: 4.2.3.2.6. The chamber is then sealed and the background hydrocarbon concentration, temper…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.6.body: The chamber is then sealed and the background hydrocarbon concentration, temperature and barometric pressure are measured. These are the initial readings C_HCi, P_i, T_i used in the enclosure background calculation.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.7.lb: 4.2.3.2.7. The enclosure is allowed to stand undisturbed with the mixing fan on for a peri…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.7.body: The enclosure is allowed to stand undisturbed with the mixing fan on for a period of four hours.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.8.lb: 4.2.3.2.8. At the end of this time the same analyser is used to measure the hydrocarbon co…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.8.body: At the end of this time the same analyser is used to measure the hydrocarbon concentration in the chamber. The temperature and the barometric pressure are also measured. These are the final readings CHCf, Pf, Tf.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.9.lb: 4.2.3.2.9. The change in mass of hydrocarbons in the enclosure shall be calculated over th…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.2.9.body: The change in mass of hydrocarbons in the enclosure shall be calculated over the time of the test in accordance with paragraph 4.2.3.4. of this annex and shall not exceed 0.05 g.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.lb: 4.2.3.3. Calibration and hydrocarbon retention test of the chamber
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.title: Calibration and hydrocarbon retention test of the chamber
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.body: The calibration and hydrocarbon retention test in the chamber provides a check on the calculated volume in paragraph 4.2.3.1. of this annex and also measures any leak rate. The enclosure leak rate shall be determined at the enclosure's introduction to service, after any operations in the enclosure which may affect the integrity of the enclosure, and at least monthly thereafter. If six consecutive monthly retention checks are successfully completed without corrective action, the enclosure leak rate may be determined quarterly thereafter as long as no corrective action is required.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.1.lb: 4.2.3.3.1. The enclosure shall be purged until a stable hydrocarbon concentration is reach…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.1.body: The enclosure shall be purged until a stable hydrocarbon concentration is reached. The mixing fan is turned on, if not already switched on. The hydrocarbon analyser is zeroed, calibrated if required, and spanned.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.2.lb: 4.2.3.3.2. On variable-volume enclosures, the enclosure shall be latched to the nominal vo…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.2.body: On variable-volume enclosures, the enclosure shall be latched to the nominal volume position. On fixed-volume enclosures the outlet and inlet flow streams shall be closed.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.3.lb: 4.2.3.3.3. The ambient temperature control system is then turned on (if not already on) an…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.3.body: The ambient temperature control system is then turned on (if not already on) and adjusted for an initial temperature of 35 °C, or at the choice of the manufacturer 36 °C.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.4.lb: 4.2.3.3.4. When the enclosure stabilises at 35 °C • 2 °C, or at the choice of the manufact…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.4.body: When the enclosure stabilises at 35 °C • 2 °C, or at the choice of the manufacturer 36 °C • 2 °C, the enclosure is sealed and the background concentration, temperature and barometric pressure measured. These are the initial readings CHCi, Pi, Ti used in the enclosure calibration.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.5.lb: 4.2.3.3.5. A quantity of approximately 4 grams of propane is injected into the enclosure. …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.5.body: A quantity of approximately 4 grams of propane is injected into the enclosure. The mass of propane shall be measured to an accuracy and precision of •2 per cent of the measured value.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.6.lb: 4.2.3.3.6. The contents of the chamber shall be allowed to mix for five minutes and then t…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.6.body: The contents of the chamber shall be allowed to mix for five minutes and then the hydrocarbon concentration, temperature and barometric pressure are measured. These are the readings C_HCf, P_f, T_f for the calibration of the enclosure as well as the initial readings C_HCi, P_i, T_i for the retention check.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.7.lb: 4.2.3.3.7. Based on the readings taken according to paragraph 4.2.3.3.4. and 4.2.3.3.6. of…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.7.body: Based on the readings taken according to paragraph 4.2.3.3.4. and 4.2.3.3.6. of this annex and the formula in paragraph 4.2.3.4. of this annex, the mass of propane in the enclosure is calculated. This shall be within ±2 per cent of the mass of propane measured in paragraph 4.2.3.3.5. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.8.lb: 4.2.3.3.8. For variable-volume enclosures the enclosure shall be unlatched from the nomina…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.8.body: For variable-volume enclosures the enclosure shall be unlatched from the nominal volume configuration. For fixed-volume enclosures, the outlet and inlet flow streams shall be opened.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.9.lb: 4.2.3.3.9. The process is then begun by cycling the ambient temperature from 35 °C to 20 °…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.9.body: The process is then begun by cycling the ambient temperature from 35 °C to 20 °C and back to 35 °C, or at the choice of the manufacturer 35.6 °C to 22.2 °C and back to 35.6 °C, over a 24-hour period according to the profile, or the alternative profile, specified in paragraph 6.5.9. of this annex within 15 minutes of sealing the enclosure. (Tolerances as specified in paragraph 6.5.9.1. of this annex.)

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.10.lb: 4.2.3.3.10. At the completion of the 24-hour cycling period, the final hydrocarbon concentr…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.10.body: At the completion of the 24-hour cycling period, the final hydrocarbon concentration, temperature and barometric pressure are measured and recorded. These are the final readings CHCf, Pf, Tf for the hydrocarbon retention check.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.11.lb: 4.2.3.3.11. Using the formula in paragraph 4.2.3.4. of this annex, the hydrocarbon mass is …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.3.11.body: Using the formula in paragraph 4.2.3.4. of this annex, the hydrocarbon mass is then calculated from the readings taken in paragraphs 4.2.3.3.6. and 4.2.3.3.10. of this annex. The mass may not differ by more than 3 per cent from the hydrocarbon mass given in paragraph 4.2.3.3.7. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.4.title: Calculations
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.2.3.4.body: The calculation of net hydrocarbon mass change within the enclosure is used to determine the chamber's hydrocarbon background and leak rate. Initial and final readings of hydrocarbon concentration, temperature and barometric pressure are used to calculate the mass change. The calculation shall be undertaken in accordance with the equation in either paragraph 7.1. or alternatively paragraph 7.1.1. of this annex, using the following value for V. V is the net enclosure volume, m.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.title: Analytical systems
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.body: The analytical systems shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 4.3.1. to. 4.3.3. of this annex. Continuous measuring of hydrocarbons is not mandatory unless the fixed volume type enclosure is used.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.1.1.lb: 4.3.1.1. The atmosphere within the chamber is monitored using a hydrocarbon detector of …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.1.1.body: The atmosphere within the chamber is monitored using a hydrocarbon detector of the FID type. Sample gas shall be drawn from the mid-point of one side wall or roof of the chamber and any bypass flow shall be returned to the enclosure, preferably to a point immediately downstream of the mixing fan.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.1.2.lb: 4.3.1.2. The hydrocarbon analyser shall have a response time to 90 per cent of final rea…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.1.2.body: The hydrocarbon analyser shall have a response time to 90 per cent of final reading of less than 1.5 seconds. Its stability shall be better than 2 per cent of full scale at zero and at 80 • 20 per cent of full scale over a 15-minute period for all operational ranges.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.1.3.lb: 4.3.1.3. The repeatability of the analyser expressed as one standard deviation shall be …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.1.3.body: The repeatability of the analyser expressed as one standard deviation shall be better than •1 per cent of full scale deflection at zero and at 80 • 20 per cent of full scale on all ranges used.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.1.4.lb: 4.3.1.4. The operational ranges of the analyser shall be chosen to give best resolution …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.1.4.body: The operational ranges of the analyser shall be chosen to give best resolution over the measurement, calibration and leak checking procedures.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.2.1.lb: 4.3.2.1. The hydrocarbon analyser shall be fitted with a device to record electrical sig…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.2.1.body: The hydrocarbon analyser shall be fitted with a device to record electrical signal output either by strip chart recorder or other data processing system at a frequency of at least once per minute. The recording system shall have operating characteristics at least equivalent to the signal being recorded and shall provide a permanent record of results. The record shall show a positive indication of the beginning and end of the hot soak or diurnal emission test (including beginning and end of sampling periods along with the time elapsed between start and completion of each test).

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.1.title: Detector response optimisation
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.1.body: The FID shall be adjusted as specified by the instrument manufacturer. Propane in air should be used to optimise the response on the most common operating range.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.title: Calibration of the hydrocarbon analyser
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.body: The analyser should be calibrated using propane in air and purified synthetic air. See paragraph 6.2. of Annex B5 of this Regulation. Each of the normally used operating ranges are calibrated in accordance with paragraphs 4.3.3.2.1. to 4.3.3.2.4. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.1.lb: 4.3.3.2.1. Establish the calibration curve by at least five calibration points spaced as e…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.1.body: Establish the calibration curve by at least five calibration points spaced as evenly as possible over the operating range. The nominal concentration of the calibration gas with the highest concentrations to be at least 80 per cent of the full scale.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.2.lb: 4.3.3.2.2. Calculate the calibration curve by the method of least squares. If the resultin…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.2.body: Calculate the calibration curve by the method of least squares. If the resulting polynomial degree is greater than 3, then the number of calibration points shall be at least the number of the polynomial degree plus 2.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.3.lb: 4.3.3.2.3. The calibration curve shall not differ by more than 2 per cent from the nominal…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.3.body: The calibration curve shall not differ by more than 2 per cent from the nominal value of each calibration gas.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.4.lb: 4.3.3.2.4. Using the coefficients of the polynomial derived from paragraph 5 of Annex B5, …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.4.body: Using the coefficients of the polynomial derived from paragraph 5 of Annex B5, a table of indicated reading against true concentration shall be drawn up in steps of no greater than 1 per cent of full scale. This is to be carried out for each analyser range calibrated. The table shall also contain other relevant data such as: (a) Date of calibration, span and zero potentiometer readings (where applicable); (b) Nominal scale; (c) Reference data of each calibration gas used; (d) The actual and indicated value of each calibration gas used together with the percentage differences; (e) FID fuel and type; (f) FID air pressure.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.5.lb: 4.3.3.2.5. If it can be shown to the satisfaction of the responsible authority that altern…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.3.3.2.5.body: If it can be shown to the satisfaction of the responsible authority that alternative technology (e.g. computer, electronically controlled range switch) can give equivalent accuracy, then those alternatives may be used.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.title: Temperature recording system
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.body: The temperature recording system shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 4.4.1. to 4.4.5. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.1.lb: 4.4.1. The temperature in the chamber is recorded at two points by temperature sensors…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.1.body: The temperature in the chamber is recorded at two points by temperature sensors which are connected so as to show a mean value. The measuring points are extended approximately 0.1 m into the enclosure from the vertical centre line of each side wall at a height of 0.9 ± 0.2 m.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.2.lb: 4.4.2. The temperatures of the fuel tank(s) are recorded by means of the sensor positi…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.2.body: The temperatures of the fuel tank(s) are recorded by means of the sensor positioned in the fuel tank as in paragraph 6.1.1. of this annex in the case of use of the gasoline canister load option (paragraph 6.5.5.3. of this annex).

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.3.lb: 4.4.3. Temperatures shall, throughout the evaporative emission measurements, be record…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.3.body: Temperatures shall, throughout the evaporative emission measurements, be recorded or entered into a data processing system at a frequency of at least once per minute.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.4.lb: 4.4.4. The accuracy of the temperature recording system shall be within •1.0 K and the…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.4.body: The accuracy of the temperature recording system shall be within •1.0 K and the temperature shall be capable of being resolved to •0.4 K.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.5.lb: 4.4.5. The recording or data processing system shall be capable of resolving time to •…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.4.5.body: The recording or data processing system shall be capable of resolving time to •15 seconds.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.5.title: Pressure recording system
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.5.body: The pressure recording system shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 4.5.1. to 4.5.3.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.5.1.lb: 4.5.1. The difference Δp between barometric pressure within the test area and the encl…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.5.1.body: The difference Δp between barometric pressure within the test area and the enclosure internal pressure shall, throughout the evaporative emission measurements, be recorded or entered into a data processing system at a frequency of at least once per minute.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.5.2.lb: 4.5.2. The accuracy of the pressure recording system shall be within •0.3 kPa and the …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.5.2.body: The accuracy of the pressure recording system shall be within •0.3 kPa and the pressure shall be capable of being resolved to •0.025 kPa.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.5.3.lb: 4.5.3. The recording or data processing system shall be capable of resolving time to •…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.5.3.body: The recording or data processing system shall be capable of resolving time to •15 seconds.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.6.title: Fans
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.6.body: The fans shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 4.6.1. and 4.6.2. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.6.1.lb: 4.6.1. By the use of one or more fans or blowers with the Sealed Housing Evaporative D…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.6.1.body: By the use of one or more fans or blowers with the Sealed Housing Evaporative Determination (SHED) door(s) open, it shall be possible to reduce the hydrocarbons concentration in the chamber to the ambient hydrocarbon level.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.6.2.lb: 4.6.2. The chamber shall have one or more fans or blowers of like capacity 0.1 to 0.5 …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.6.2.body: The chamber shall have one or more fans or blowers of like capacity 0.1 to 0.5 m3/sec. with which to thoroughly mix the atmosphere in the enclosure. It shall be possible to attain an even temperature and hydrocarbon concentration in the chamber during measurements. The vehicle in the enclosure shall not be subjected to a direct stream of air from the fans or blowers.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.7.title: Calibration gases
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.7.body: The gases shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 4.7.1. and 4.7.2. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.7.1.lb: 4.7.1. The following pure gases shall be available for calibration and operation: Puri…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.7.1.body: The following pure gases shall be available for calibration and operation: Purified synthetic air: (purity < 1 ppm C1 equivalent, •1 ppm CO, • 400 ppm CO2, • 0.1 ppm NO; oxygen content between 18 and 21 per cent by volume). Hydrocarbon analyser fuel gas: defined in paragraph 6.1.2.4. of Annex B5 to this Regulation or (40 • 2 per cent hydrogen, and balance helium with less than 1 ppm C1 equivalent hydrocarbon, less than 400 ppm CO2), Propane (C3H8): 99.5 per cent minimum purity. Butane (C4H10): 98 per cent minimum purity. Nitrogen (N2): defined in paragraph 6.1.2.1. of Annex B5 to this Regulation or 98 per cent minimum purity.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.7.2.lb: 4.7.2. Calibration and span gases shall be available containing mixtures of propane (C…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.7.2.body: Calibration and span gases shall be available containing mixtures of propane (C3H8) and purified synthetic air. The true concentrations of a calibration gas shall be within 2 per cent of the stated figures. The accuracy of the diluted gases obtained when using a gas divider shall be to within •2 per cent of the true value. The concentrations specified in paragraphs 4.2.3. and 4.3.3. of this annex may also be obtained by the use of a gas divider using synthetic air as the dilutant gas.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.8.lb: 4.8. Carbon canister weighing scale for depressurisation puff loss overflow measurem…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.8.body: Carbon canister weighing scale for depressurisation puff loss overflow measurement The carbon canister weighing scale shall have an accuracy of ±0.02 g.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.9.lb: 4.9. Fuel tank heating (applicable for gasoline canister load option only)
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.9.title: Fuel tank heating (applicable for gasoline canister load option only)

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.9.1.lb: 4.9.1. The fuel in the vehicle tank(s) shall be heated by a controllable source of hea…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.9.1.body: The fuel in the vehicle tank(s) shall be heated by a controllable source of heat; for example a heating pad of 2,000 W capacity is suitable. The heating system shall apply heat evenly to the tank walls beneath the level of the fuel so as not to cause local overheating of the fuel. Heat shall not be applied to the vapour in the tank above the fuel.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.9.2.lb: 4.9.2. The tank heating device shall make it possible to heat the fuel in the tank eve…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.9.2.body: The tank heating device shall make it possible to heat the fuel in the tank evenly by 14 °C from 16 °C within 60 minutes, with the temperature sensor position as in paragraph 4.9.3. of this annex. The heating system shall be capable of controlling the fuel temperature to •1.5 °C of the required temperature during the tank heating process.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.9.3.lb: 4.9.3. The fuel tank of the vehicle shall, without introducing any leaks, be equipped …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.4.9.3.body: The fuel tank of the vehicle shall, without introducing any leaks, be equipped with a temperature sensor to enable the temperature to be measured at the midpoint of the fuel in the fuel tank when filled to 40 per cent of its capacity.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.lb: 5. Procedure for carbon canister bench ageing and PF determination
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.title: Procedure for carbon canister bench ageing and PF determination

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.title: Carbon canister bench ageing
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.body: Before performing the hot soak and diurnal losses sequences, the carbon canister shall be aged according to the procedure described in Figure C3/1. [FIGURE:REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.FIG-C3/1]

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.1.lb: 5.1.1. Ageing through exposure to temperature cycling
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.1.title: Ageing through exposure to temperature cycling
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.1.body: The carbon canister shall be cycled between temperatures from -15 °C to 60 °C in a dedicated temperature enclosure with 30 minutes of stabilisation at -15 °C and 60 °C. Each cycle shall last 210 minutes (see Figure C3/2). The temperature gradient shall be as close as possible to 1 °C/min. No forced air flow should pass through the carbon canister. The cycle shall be repeated 50 times consecutively. In total, this procedure lasts 175 hours. [FIGURE:REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.FIG-C3/2]

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.2.title: Ageing through exposure to vibration
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.2.body: Following the temperature ageing procedure, the carbon canister shall be shaken vertically with the carbon canister mounted as per its orientation in the vehicle with an overall Grms (root mean square acceleration) > 1.5 m/sec with a frequency of 30 ±10 Hz. The test shall last 12 hours.
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.2.foot: correction as referred to in Appendix 2 to Annex B6 of this Regulation for ICE vehicles, and Appendix 2 to Annex B8 of this Regulation for HEVs (K_CO2)

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.lb: 5.1.3. Ageing through exposure to fuel vapour and determining BWC300
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.title: Ageing through exposure to fuel vapour and determining BWC300

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.lb: 5.1.3.1. Ageing shall consist of repeatedly loading with fuel vapour and purging with la…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.body: Ageing shall consist of repeatedly loading with fuel vapour and purging with laboratory air.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.1.lb: 5.1.3.1.1. After temperature and vibration ageing, the carbon canister shall be further ag…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.1.body: After temperature and vibration ageing, the carbon canister shall be further aged with a mixture of market fuel as specified in paragraph 5.1.3.1.1.1. of this annex and nitrogen or air with a 50 ±15 per cent fuel vapour volume. The fuel vapour fill rate shall be 60 ±20 g/h. The carbon canister shall be loaded to 2 gram breakthrough. Alternatively, loading shall be considered to be completed when the hydrocarbon concentration level at the vent outlet reaches 3,000 ppm.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.1.1.lb: 5.1.3.1.1.1. The market fuel used for this test shall fulfil the same requirements as a refe…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.1.1.body: The market fuel used for this test shall fulfil the same requirements as a reference fuel with respect to: (a) Density at 15 °C; (b) Vapour pressure; (c) Distillation (70 °C, 100 °C, 150 °C); (d) Hydrocarbon analysis (olefins, aromatics, benzene only); (e) Oxygen content; (f) Ethanol content.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.2.lb: 5.1.3.1.2. The carbon canister shall be purged between 5 and 60 minutes after loading with…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.2.body: The carbon canister shall be purged between 5 and 60 minutes after loading with 25 ±5 litres per minute of emission laboratory air until 300 bed volume exchanges are reached.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.3.lb: 5.1.3.1.3. The procedures set out in paragraphs 5.1.3.1.1. and 5.1.3.1.2. of this annex sh…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.3.body: The procedures set out in paragraphs 5.1.3.1.1. and 5.1.3.1.2. of this annex shall be repeated 300 times after which the carbon canister shall be considered to be stabilised.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.4.lb: 5.1.3.1.4. The procedure to measure the butane working capacity (BWC) with respect to the …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.1.4.body: The procedure to measure the butane working capacity (BWC) with respect to the evaporative emission family in paragraph 6.6.3. of this Regulation shall consist of the following. (a) The stabilised carbon canister shall be loaded to 2 gram breakthrough and subsequently purged a minimum of 5 times. Loading shall be performed with a mixture composed of 50 per cent butane and 50 per cent nitrogen by volume at a rate of 40 grams butane per hour. (b) Purging shall be performed according to paragraph 5.1.3.1.2. of this annex. (c) The BWC shall be recorded after each loading. (d) BWC300 shall be calculated as the average of the last 5 BWCs.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.2.lb: 5.1.3.2. If the aged carbon canister is provided by a supplier, the vehicle manufacturer…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.2.body: If the aged carbon canister is provided by a supplier, the vehicle manufacturer shall inform the responsible authority in advance of the ageing process to enable the witnessing of any part of that process.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.3.lb: 5.1.3.3. The manufacturer shall provide the responsible authority a test report includin…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.1.3.3.body: The manufacturer shall provide the responsible authority a test report including at least the following elements: (a) Type of activated carbon; (b) Loading rate; (c) Fuel specifications.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.lb: 5.2. Determination of the PF of the fuel tank system (see Figure C3/3)
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.title: Determination of the PF of the fuel tank system (see Figure C3/3)

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.1.lb: 5.2.1. The fuel tank system representative of a family shall be selected and mounted o…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.1.body: The fuel tank system representative of a family shall be selected and mounted on a rig in a similar orientation as in the vehicle. The tank shall be filled to 40 ±2 per cent of its nominal capacity with reference fuel at a temperature of 18 °C ±2 °C. The rig with the fuel tank system shall be placed in a room with a controlled temperature of 40 °C ±2 °C for 3 weeks.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.2.lb: 5.2.2. At the end of the third week, the tank shall be drained and refilled with refer…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.2.body: At the end of the third week, the tank shall be drained and refilled with reference fuel at a temperature of 18 °C ±2 °C to 40 ±2 per cent of its nominal capacity. Within 6 to 36 hours, the rig with the fuel tank system shall be placed in an enclosure. The last 6 hours of this period shall be at an ambient temperature of 20 °C ±2 °C. In the enclosure, a diurnal procedure shall be performed over the first 24-hour period of the procedure described in paragraph 6.5.9. of this annex. The fuel vapour in the tank shall be vented to the outside of the enclosure to eliminate the possibility of the tank venting emissions being counted as [TABLE:REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.2.TABLE-U1] permeation. The HC emissions shall be measured and the value shall be recorded as HC3W.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.3.lb: 5.2.3. The rig with the fuel tank system shall be placed again in a room with a contro…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.3.body: The rig with the fuel tank system shall be placed again in a room with a controlled temperature of 40 °C ±2 °C for the remaining 17 weeks.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.4.lb: 5.2.4. At the end of the seventeenth week, the tank shall be drained and refilled with…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.4.body: At the end of the seventeenth week, the tank shall be drained and refilled with reference fuel at a temperature of 18 °C ±2 °C to 40 ±2 per cent of its nominal tank capacity. Within 6 to 36 hours, the rig with the fuel tank system shall be placed in an enclosure. The last 6 hours of this period shall be at an ambient temperature of 20 °C ±2 °C. In the enclosure, a diurnal procedure shall be performed over a first period of 24 hours of the procedure described according to paragraph 6.5.9. of this annex. The fuel tank system shall be vented to the outside of the enclosure to eliminate the possibility of the tank venting emissions being counted as permeation. The HC emissions shall be measured and the value shall be recorded in this case as HC_20W.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.5.lb: 5.2.5. The PF is the difference between HC_20W and HC_3W in g/24h calculated to 3 sign…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.5.body: The PF is the difference between HC_20W and HC_3W in g/24h calculated to 3 significant digits using the following equation: [EQ:REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.5.EQ-1]

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.6.lb: 5.2.6. If the PF is determined by a supplier, the vehicle manufacturer shall inform th…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.6.body: If the PF is determined by a supplier, the vehicle manufacturer shall inform the responsible authority in advance of the determination to allow witness check in the supplier’s facility.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.7.lb: 5.2.7. The manufacturer shall provide the responsible authority with a test report con…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.7.body: The manufacturer shall provide the responsible authority with a test report containing at least the following: (a) A full description of the fuel tank system tested, including information on the type of tank tested, whether the tank is metal, monolayer nonmetal or multilayer, and which types of materials are used for the tank and other parts of the fuel tank system; (b) The weekly mean temperatures at which the ageing was performed; (c) The HC measured at week 3 (HC_3W); (d) The HC measured at week 20 (HC20W); (e) The resulting permeability factor (PF).

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.8.lb: 5.2.8. As an alternative to paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.7. inclusive of this annex, a man…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.5.2.8.body: As an alternative to paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.7. inclusive of this annex, a manufacturer using multilayer tanks or metal tanks may choose to use an Assigned Permeability Factor (APF) instead of performing the complete measurement procedure mentioned above: APF multilayer/metal tank = 120 mg /24 h Where the manufacturer chooses to use an APF, the manufacturer shall provide the responsible authority with a declaration in which the type of tank is clearly specified as well as a declaration of the type of materials used.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.lb: 6. Test procedure for the measurement of hot soak and diurnal losses
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.title: Test procedure for the measurement of hot soak and diurnal losses

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.1.title: Vehicle preparation
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.1.body: The vehicle shall be prepared in accordance with paragraphs 6.1.1. and 6.1.2. of this annex. At the request of the manufacturer and with approval of the responsible authority, non-fuel background emission sources (e.g. paint, adhesives, plastics, fuel/vapour lines, tyres, and other rubber or polymer components) may be reduced to typical vehicle ba ckground levels before testing (e.g. baking of tyres at temperatures of 50 °C or higher for appropriate periods, baking of the vehicle, draining washer fluid). For a sealed fuel tank system, the vehicle carbon canisters shall be installed so that access to carbon canisters and connection/disconnection of carbon canisters can be done easily.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.1.1.lb: 6.1.1. The vehicle shall be mechanically prepared before the test as follows: (a) The …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.1.1.body: The vehicle shall be mechanically prepared before the test as follows: (a) The exhaust system of the vehicle shall not exhibit any leaks. Openings in the exhaust system designed to remove condensate as described in paragraph 2.4.3. of Annex B6 shall be sealed prior to the test; (b) The vehicle may be steam-cleaned before the test; (c) In the case of use of the gasoline canister load option (paragraph 6.5.5.3. of this annex) the fuel tank of the vehicle shall be equipped with a temperature sensor to enable the temperature to be measured at the midpoint of the fuel in the fuel tank when filled to 40 per cent of its capacity; (d) Additional fittings, adapters or devices may be fitted to the fuel system in order to allow a complete draining of the fuel tank. For this purpose it is not necessary to modify the shell of the tank; (e) The manufacturer may propose a test method in order to take into account the loss of hydrocarbons by evaporation coming only from the fuel system of the vehicle.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.1.2.lb: 6.1.2. The vehicle is taken into the test area where the ambient temperature is betwee…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.1.2.body: The vehicle is taken into the test area where the ambient temperature is between 20 and 30 °C.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.2.lb: 6.2. Mode selections and gear shift prescriptions
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.2.title: Mode selections and gear shift prescriptions

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.2.1.lb: 6.2.1. For vehicles with manual shift transmissions, the gear shift prescriptions spec…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.2.1.body: For vehicles with manual shift transmissions, the gear shift prescriptions specified in Annex B2 shall apply.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.2.2.lb: 6.2.2. In the case of pure ICE vehicles, the mode shall be selected according to Annex…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.2.2.body: In the case of pure ICE vehicles, the mode shall be selected according to Annex B6.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.2.3.lb: 6.2.3. In the case of NOVC-HEVs and OVC-HEVs, the mode shall be selected according to …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.2.3.body: In the case of NOVC-HEVs and OVC-HEVs, the mode shall be selected according to Appendix 6 to Annex B8.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.2.4.lb: 6.2.4. Upon request of the responsible authority, the selected mode may be different f…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.2.4.body: Upon request of the responsible authority, the selected mode may be different from that described in paragraphs 6.2.2. and 6.2.3. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.3.title: Test conditions
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.3.body: The tests included in this annex shall be performed using the test conditions specific to interpolation family vehicle H with the highest cycle energy demand of all the interpolation families included in the evaporative emission family being considered. Otherwise, at the request of the responsible authority, any cycle energy representative of a vehicle in the family may be used for the test.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.4.title: Flow of the test procedure
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.4.body: The test procedure for non-sealed and sealed tank systems shall be followed according to the flow chart described in Figure C3/4. The sealed fuel tank systems shall be tested with one of 2 options. One option is to test the vehicle with one continuous procedure. Another option, called the 'stand-alone test procedure', is to test the vehicle with two separate procedures which will allow repeating the dynamometer test and the diurnal tests without repeating the tank depressurisation puff loss overflow test and the depressurisation puff loss measurement. [FIGURE:REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.FIG-C3/4] fuel tanks continuous and sealed fuel tanks stand-alone puff loss alone hot soak and diurnals [TABLE:REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.4.TABLE-U1]

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.lb: 6.5. Continuous test procedure for non-sealed fuel tank systems
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.title: Continuous test procedure for non-sealed fuel tank systems

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.1.title: Fuel drain and refill
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.1.body: The fuel tank of the vehicle shall be emptied. This shall be done so as not to abnormally purge or abnormally load the evaporative control devices fitted to the vehicle. Removal of the fuel cap is normally sufficient to achieve this. The fuel tank shall be refilled with reference fuel at a temperature of 18 °C ±2 °C to 40 ±2 per cent of its nominal capacity.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.2.title: Soak
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.2.body: Within 5 minutes after completing the fuel drain and refill, the vehicle shall be soaked for a minimum of 6 hours and a maximum of 36 hours at 23 °C ±3 °C.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.3.title: Preconditioning drive
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.3.body: The vehicle shall be placed on a chassis dynamometer and driven over the following phases of the cycle described in Annex B1: (a) For Class 1 vehicles: low, medium, low, low, medium, low (b) For Class 2 and 3 vehicles: low, medium, high, medium. For OVC-HEVs, the preconditioning drive shall be performed under the charge-sustaining operating condition as defined in paragraph 3.3.6. of this Regulation. Upon the request of responsible authority, any other mode may be used.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.4.title: Fuel drain and refill
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.4.body: Within one hour after the preconditioning drive, the fuel tank of the vehicle shall be emptied. This shall be done so as not to abnormally purge or abnormally load the evaporative control devices fitted to the vehicle. Removal of the fuel cap is normally sufficient to achieve this. The fuel tank shall be refilled with test fuel at a temperature of 18 °C ±2 °C to 40 ±2 per cent of its nominal capacity.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.title: Soak
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.body: Within five minutes of completing fuel drain and refill, the vehicle shall be parked for a minimum of 12 hours and a maximum of 36 hours at 23 °C ±3 °C. During soaking, the procedures described in paragraphs 6.5.5.1. and 6.5.5.2. of this annex may be performed either in the order of first paragraph 6.5.5.1. followed by paragraph 6.5.5.2. or in the order paragraph 6.5.5.2. followed by paragraph 6.5.5.1. The procedures described in paragraphs 6.5.5.1. and 6.5.5.2. may also be performed simultaneously.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.1.title: REESS charge
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.1.body: For OVC-HEVs, the REESS shall be fully charged according to the charging requirements described in paragraph 2.2.3. of Appendix 4 to Annex B8.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.2.title: Carbon canister loading
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.2.body: The carbon canister aged according to the sequence described in paragraph 5.1. to 5.1.3.1.3. inclusive of this annex shall be loaded to 2 gram breakthrough according to the procedure described in paragraph 6.5.5.2.1. of this annex. One of the methods specified in paragraphs 6.5.5.3. and 6.5.5.4. of this annex shall be used to precondition the evaporative canister. For vehicles with multiple canisters, each canister shall be preconditioned separately.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.2.1.lb: 6.5.5.2.1. Canister emissions are measured to determine breakthrough. Breakthrough is here…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.2.1.body: Canister emissions are measured to determine breakthrough. Breakthrough is here defined as the point at which the cumulative quantity of hydrocarbons emitted is equal to 2 grams.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.2.2.lb: 6.5.5.2.2. Breakthrough may be verified using the evaporative emission enclosure as descri…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.2.2.body: Breakthrough may be verified using the evaporative emission enclosure as described in paragraphs 6.5.5.3. and 6.5.5.4. of this annex. Alternatively, breakthrough may be determined by using an auxiliary evaporative canister connected downstream of the vehicle's canister. The auxiliary canister shall be well purged with dry air prior to loading.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.2.3.lb: 6.5.5.2.3. The measuring chamber shall be purged for several minutes immediately before th…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.2.3.body: The measuring chamber shall be purged for several minutes immediately before the test until a stable background is obtained. The chamber air mixing fan(s) shall be switched on at this time. The hydrocarbon analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the test.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.lb: 6.5.5.3. Canister loading with repeated heat builds to breakthrough
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.title: Canister loading with repeated heat builds to breakthrough

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.1.lb: 6.5.5.3.1. The fuel tank(s) of the vehicle(s) is (are) emptied using the fuel tank drain(s…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.1.body: The fuel tank(s) of the vehicle(s) is (are) emptied using the fuel tank drain(s). This shall be done so as not to abnormally purge or abnormally load the evaporative control devices fitted to the vehicle. Removal of the fuel cap is normally sufficient to achieve this.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.2.lb: 6.5.5.3.2. The fuel tank(s) is (are) refilled with test fuel at a temperature of between 1…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.2.body: The fuel tank(s) is (are) refilled with test fuel at a temperature of between 10 to 14 °C to 40 • 2 per cent of the tank's normal volumetric capacity. The fuel cap(s) of the vehicle shall be fitted at this point.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.3.lb: 6.5.5.3.3. Within one hour of being refuelled the vehicle shall be placed, with the engine…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.3.body: Within one hour of being refuelled the vehicle shall be placed, with the engine shut off, in the evaporative emission enclosure. The fuel tank temperature sensor is connected to the temperature recording system. A heat source shall be properly positioned with respect to the fuel tank(s) and connected to the temperature controller. The heat source is specified in paragraph 4.9. of this annex. In the case of vehicles fitted with more than one fuel tank, all the tanks shall be heated in the same way as described below. The temperatures of the tanks shall be identical to within •1.5 °C.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.4.lb: 6.5.5.3.4. The fuel may be artificially heated to the starting diurnal temperature of 20 °…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.4.body: The fuel may be artificially heated to the starting diurnal temperature of 20 °C • 1 °C.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.5.lb: 6.5.5.3.5. When the fuel temperature reaches at least 19 °C, the following steps shall be …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.5.body: When the fuel temperature reaches at least 19 °C, the following steps shall be taken immediately: the purge blower shall be turned off; enclosure doors closed and sealed; and measurement initiated of the hydrocarbon level in the enclosure.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.6.lb: 6.5.5.3.6. When the fuel temperature of the fuel tank reaches 20 °C a linear heat build of…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.6.body: When the fuel temperature of the fuel tank reaches 20 °C a linear heat build of 15 °C begins. The fuel shall be heated in such a way that the temperature of the fuel during the heating conforms to the function below to within •1.5 °C. The elapsed time of the heat build and temperature rise is recorded. T_r = T_o + 0.2333 x t Where: Tr = required temperature (K), To = initial temperature (K), t = time from start of the tank heat build in minutes.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.7.lb: 6.5.5.3.7. As soon as break-through occurs or when the fuel temperature reaches 35 °C, whi…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.3.7.body: As soon as break-through occurs or when the fuel temperature reaches 35 °C, whichever occurs first, the heat source is turned off, the enclosure doors unsealed and opened, and the vehicle fuel tank cap(s) removed. If breakthrough has not occurred by the time the fuel temperature 35 °C, the heat source is removed from the vehicle, the vehicle removed from the evaporative emission enclosure and the entire procedure outlined in paragraph 6.6.1.2. of this annex repeated until breakthrough occurs.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.4.1.lb: 6.5.5.4.1. If the enclosure is used for the determination of the break-through (see paragr…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.4.1.body: If the enclosure is used for the determination of the break-through (see paragraph 6.5.5.2.2. of this annex) the vehicle shall be placed, with the engine shut off, in the evaporative emission enclosure.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.4.2.lb: 6.5.5.4.2. The evaporative emission canister shall be prepared for the canister loading op…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.4.2.body: The evaporative emission canister shall be prepared for the canister loading operation. The canister shall not be removed from the vehicle, unless access to it in its normal location is so restricted that loading can only reasonably be accomplished by removing the canister from the vehicle. Special care shall be taken during this step to avoid damage to the components and the integrity of the fuel system.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.4.3.lb: 6.5.5.4.3. The canister is loaded with a mixture composed of 50 per cent butane and 50 per…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.4.3.body: The canister is loaded with a mixture composed of 50 per cent butane and 50 per cent nitrogen by volume at a rate of 40 grams butane per hour.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.4.4.lb: 6.5.5.4.4. As soon as the canister reaches breakthrough, the vapour source shall be shut o…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.4.4.body: As soon as the canister reaches breakthrough, the vapour source shall be shut off.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.4.5.lb: 6.5.5.4.5. The evaporative emission canister shall then be reconnected and the vehicle res…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.5.4.5.body: The evaporative emission canister shall then be reconnected and the vehicle restored to its normal operating condition.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.6.title: Dynamometer test
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.6.body: The test vehicle shall be pushed onto a dynamometer and shall be driven over the cycles described in paragraph 6.5.3.(a) or paragraph 6.5.3.(b) of this annex. OVC-HEVs shall be operated in charge-depleting operating condition. The engine shall be subsequently shut off. Exhaust emissions may be sampled during this operation and the results may be used for the purpose of exhaust emission and fuel consumption type approval if this operation meets the requirement described in Annex B6 or Annex B8.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.title: Hot soak evaporative emissions test
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.body: Within 7 minutes after the dynamometer test and within 2 minutes of the engine being switched off, the hot soak evaporative emissions test shall be performed in accordance with paragraphs 6.5.7.1. to 6.5.7.8. of this annex. The hot soak losses shall be calculated according to paragraph 7.1. of this annex and recorded as M_HS.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.1.lb: 6.5.7.1. Before the completion of the test run the measuring chamber shall be purged for…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.1.body: Before the completion of the test run the measuring chamber shall be purged for several minutes until a stable hydrocarbon background is obtained. The enclosure mixing fan(s) shall also be turned on at this time.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.2.lb: 6.5.7.2. The hydrocarbon analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately prior to the t…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.2.body: The hydrocarbon analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately prior to the test.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.3.lb: 6.5.7.3. At the end of the driving cycle the engine bonnet shall be completely closed an…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.3.body: At the end of the driving cycle the engine bonnet shall be completely closed and all connections between the vehicle and the test stand disconnected. The vehicle is then driven to the measuring chamber with a minimum use of the accelerator pedal. The engine shall be turned off before any part of the vehicle enters the measuring chamber. The time at which the engine is switched off is recorded on the evaporative emission measurement data recording system and temperature recording begins. The vehicle's windows and luggage compartments shall be opened at this stage, if not already opened.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.4.lb: 6.5.7.4. The vehicle shall be pushed or otherwise moved into the measuring chamber with …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.4.body: The vehicle shall be pushed or otherwise moved into the measuring chamber with the engine switched off.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.5.lb: 6.5.7.5. The enclosure doors are closed and sealed gas-tight within two minutes of the e…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.5.body: The enclosure doors are closed and sealed gas-tight within two minutes of the engine being switched off and within seven minutes of the end of the conditioning drive.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.6.lb: 6.5.7.6. The start of a 60 • 0.5 minute hot soak period begins when the chamber is seale…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.6.body: The start of a 60 • 0.5 minute hot soak period begins when the chamber is sealed. The hydrocarbon concentration, temperature and barometric pressure are measured to give the initial readings CHCi, Pi and Ti for the hot soak test. These figures are used in the evaporative emission calculation, paragraph 6. The ambient temperature T of the enclosure shall not be less than 23 °C and no more than 31 °C during the 60-minute hot soak period.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.7.lb: 6.5.7.7. The hydrocarbon analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the end…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.7.body: The hydrocarbon analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the end of the 60 • 0.5 minute test period.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.8.lb: 6.5.7.8. At the end of the 60 • 0.5 minute test period, the hydrocarbon concentration in…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.7.8.body: At the end of the 60 • 0.5 minute test period, the hydrocarbon concentration in the chamber shall be measured. The temperature and the barometric pressure are also measured. These are the final readings C_HCf, P_f and T_f for the hot soak test used for the calculation in paragraph 6. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.8.title: Soak
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.8.body: After the hot soak evaporative emissions test, the test vehicle shall be soaked for not less than 6 hours and not more than 36 hours between the end of the hot soak test and the start of the diurnal emission test. For at least the last 6 hours of this period the vehicle shall be soaked at 20 °C ±2 °C.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.1.lb: 6.5.9.1. The test vehicle shall be exposed to two cycles of ambient temperature in accor…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.1.body: The test vehicle shall be exposed to two cycles of ambient temperature in accordance with the profile specified in Table C3/1 with a maximum deviation of •2 °C at any time. The average temperature deviation from the profile, calculated using the absolute value of each measured deviation, shall not exceed •1 °C. Ambient temperature shall be measured and recorded at least every minute. Temperature cycling shall begin at time T_start = 0, as specified in paragraph 6.5.9.6. of this annex. [TABLE:REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.TABLE-C3/1]

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.2.lb: 6.5.9.2. The enclosure shall be purged for several minutes immediately before the test u…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.2.body: The enclosure shall be purged for several minutes immediately before the test until a stable background is obtained. The chamber mixing fan(s) shall also be switched on at this time.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.3.lb: 6.5.9.3. The test vehicle, with the powertrain shut off and the test vehicle windows and…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.3.body: The test vehicle, with the powertrain shut off and the test vehicle windows and luggage compartment(s) opened, shall be moved into the measuring chamber. The mixing fan(s) shall be adjusted in such a way as to maintain a minimum air circulation speed of 8 km/h under the fuel tank of the test vehicle.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.4.lb: 6.5.9.4. The hydrocarbon analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the tes…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.4.body: The hydrocarbon analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the test.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.5.lb: 6.5.9.5. The enclosure doors shall be closed and sealed gas-tight.
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.5.body: The enclosure doors shall be closed and sealed gas-tight.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.6.lb: 6.5.9.6. Within 10 minutes of closing and sealing the doors, the hydrocarbon concentrati…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.6.body: Within 10 minutes of closing and sealing the doors, the hydrocarbon concentration, temperature and barometric pressure shall be measured to give initial readings of hydrocarbon concentration in the enclosure (C_HCi), barometric pressure (P_i) and ambient chamber temperature (T_i) for the diurnal testing. T_start = 0 starts at this time.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.7.lb: 6.5.9.7. The hydrocarbon analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the end…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.7.body: The hydrocarbon analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the end of each emission sampling period.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.8.lb: 6.5.9.8. The end of the first and second emission sampling period shall occur at 24 hour…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.5.9.8.body: The end of the first and second emission sampling period shall occur at 24 hours •6 minutes and 48 hours •6 minutes, respectively, after the beginning of the initial sampling, as specified in paragraph 6.5.9.6. of this annex. The elapsed time shall be recorded. At the end of each emission sampling period, the hydrocarbon concentration, temperature and barometric pressure shall be measured and used to calculate the diurnal test results using the equation in paragraph 7.1. of this annex. The result obtained from the first 24 hours shall be recorded as MD1. The result obtained from the second 24 hours shall be recorded as MD2.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.lb: 6.6. Continuous test procedure for sealed fuel tank systems
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.title: Continuous test procedure for sealed fuel tank systems

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.lb: 6.6.1. In the case that the fuel tank relief pressure is greater than or equal to 30 k…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.title: In the case that the fuel tank relief pressure is greater than or equal to 30 kPa

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.1.lb: 6.6.1.1. The test shall be performed as described in paragraphs 6.5.1. to 6.5.3. inclusi…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.1.body: The test shall be performed as described in paragraphs 6.5.1. to 6.5.3. inclusive of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.2.title: Fuel drain and refill
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.2.body: Within one hour after the preconditioning drive, the fuel tank of the vehicle shall be emptied. This shall be done so as not to abnormally purge or abnormally load the evaporative control devices fitted to the vehicle. Removal of the fuel cap is normally sufficient to achieve this, otherwise the carbon canister shall be disconnected. The fuel tank shall be refilled with reference fuel at a temperature of 18 °C ±2 °C to 15 ±2 per cent of the tank's nominal capacity. The operations described in paragraphs 6.6.1.3., 6.6.1.4. and 6.6.1.5. of this annex shall be completed within a total of 36 hours and for the operations described in paragraphs 6.6.1.4. and 6.6.1.5. the vehicle shall not be exposed to temperatures above 25°C.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.3.title: Soak
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.3.body: Within 5 minutes after completing fuel drain and refill, the vehicle shall be soaked for stabilisation for at least 6 hours at an ambient temperature of 20 °C ±2 °C.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.4.title: Fuel tank depressurisation
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.4.body: The tank pressure shall be subsequently released so as not to abnormally raise the inside pressure of the fuel tank. This may be done by opening the fuel cap of the vehicle. Regardless of the method of depressurisation, the vehicle shall be returned to its original condition within 1 minute.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.5.title: Carbon canister loading and purge
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.5.body: The carbon canister aged in accordance with the sequence described in paragraph 5.1. to 5.1.3.1.3. inclusive of this annex shall be loaded to 2 gram breakthrough according to the procedure described in paragraphs 6.5.5.4. to 6.5.5.4.5. inclusive to this annex, and shall be subsequently purged with 25 ±5 litres per minute with emission laboratory air. The volume of purge air shall not exceed the volume determined in accordance with the requirements of paragraph 6.6.1.5.1. This loading and purging can be done either (a) using an on-board carbon canister at a temperature of 20 °C or optionally 23 °C, or (b) by disconnecting the carbon canister. In both cases, no further relief of the tank pressure is allowed.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.5.1.title: Determination of maximum purge volume
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.5.1.body: The maximum purge amount Vol_max shall be determined by the following equation. In the case of OVC-HEVs, the vehicle shall be operated in chargesustaining operating condition. This determination can also be done at a separate test or during the preconditioning drive. [EQ:REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.5.1.EQ-1] where: is the cumulative purge volume rounded to the nearest 0.1 litres measured using a suitable device (e.g. flowmeter connected to the vent of the carbon canister or equivalent) over the cold start preconditioning drive described in the paragraph 6.5.3. of this annex, l; Vol_tank is the manufacturer’s nominal fuel tank capacity, l; FC_Pcycle is the fuel consumption over the single purge cycle described in paragraph 6.5.3. of this annex which may be measured in either warm or cold start condition, l/100 km. For OVC-HEVs and NOVC-HEVs, fuel consumption shall be calculated according to paragraph 4.2.1. of Annex B8 of this Regulation; Dist_Pcycle is the theoretical distance to the nearest 0.1 km of a single purge cycle described in paragraph 6.5.3. of this annex, km.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.6.lb: 6.6.1.6. Preparation of carbon canister depressurisation puff loss loading
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.6.title: Preparation of carbon canister depressurisation puff loss loading
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.6.body: After completing carbon canister loading and purging, the test vehicle shall be moved into an enclosure, either a SHED or an appropriate climatic chamber. It shall be demonstrated that the system is leak-free and the pressurisation is performed in a normal way during the test or by a separate test (e.g. by means of pressure sensor on the vehicle). The test vehicle shall be subsequently exposed to the first 11 hours of the ambient temperature profile specified for the diurnal emission test in Table C3/1 with a maximum deviation of •2 °C at any time. The average temperature deviation from the profile, calculated using the absolute value of each measured deviation, shall not exceed •1 °C. The ambient temperature shall be measured and recorded at least every 10 minutes.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.7.1.title: Fuel tank depressurisation before refuelling
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.7.1.body: The manufacturer shall ensure that the refuelling operation cannot be initiated before the sealed fuel tank system is fully depressurised to a pressure less than 2.5 kPa above ambient pressure in normal vehicle operation and use. At the request of the responsible authority, the manufacturer shall provide detailed information or demonstrate proof of operation (e.g. by means of pressure sensor on the vehicle). Any other technical solution may be allowed provided that a safe refuelling operation is ensured and that no excessive emissions are released to the atmosphere before the refuelling device is connected to the vehicle.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.7.2.lb: 6.6.1.7.2. Within 15 minutes after the ambient temperature has reached 35 °C, the tank rel…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.7.2.body: Within 15 minutes after the ambient temperature has reached 35 °C, the tank relief valve shall be opened to load the carbon canister. This loading procedure may be performed either inside or outside an enclosure. The carbon canister loaded according to this paragraph shall be disconnected and shall be kept in the soak area.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.8.lb: 6.6.1.8. Measurement of depressurisation puff loss overflow
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.8.title: Measurement of depressurisation puff loss overflow
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.8.body: The depressurisation puff loss overflow shall be measured using the process in either paragraph 6.6.1.8.1. or 6.6.1.8.2. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.8.1.lb: 6.6.1.8.1. The depressurisation puff loss overflow from the vehicle carbon canister may be…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.8.1.body: The depressurisation puff loss overflow from the vehicle carbon canister may be measured by using an additional carbon canister identical to the vehicle's carbon canister but not necessarily aged. The additional carbon canister shall be fully purged with dry air prior to loading and shall be connected directly at the outlet of the vehicle's canister with the shortest possible tube. The additional carbon canister shall be weighed before and after the procedure described in paragraph 6.6.1.7. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.8.2.lb: 6.6.1.8.2. The depressurisation puff loss overflow from the vehicle carbon canister during…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.8.2.body: The depressurisation puff loss overflow from the vehicle carbon canister during its depressurisation may be measured using a SHED. Within 15 minutes after the ambient temperature has reached 35°C as described in paragraph 6.6.1.6. of this annex, the chamber shall be sealed and the measurement procedure shall be started. The hydrocarbon analyser shall be zeroed and spanned, after which the hydrocarbon concentration (CHCi), temperature (Ti) and barometric pressure (Pi) shall be measured to give the initial readings CHCi, Pi and Ti for the sealed tank depressurisation puff loss overflow determination. The ambient temperature T of the enclosure shall not be less than 25°C during the measurement procedure. At the end of the procedure described in paragraph 6.6.1.7.2. of this annex, the hydrocarbon concentration (CHCf) in the chamber shall be measured after 300 ± 5 seconds. The temperature (Tf) and the barometric pressure (Pf) shall also be measured. These are the final readings CHCf, Pf and Tf for the sealed tank depressurisation puff loss overflow. The sealed tank puff loss overflow result shall be calculated according to paragraph 7.1. of this annex and recorded.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.8.3.lb: 6.6.1.8.3. There shall be no change in weight of the additional carbon canister when testi…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.8.3.body: There shall be no change in weight of the additional carbon canister when testing according to paragraph 6.6.1.8.1. or the result of the SHED measurement when testing according to paragraph 6.6.1.8.2., within the tolerance of ± 0.5 gram.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.9.title: Soak
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.9.body: After completing puff loss loading the vehicle carbon canister shall be replaced with a dummy carbon canister (of the same specification as the original but not necessarily aged), the vehicle shall then be soaked at 23 ±3 °C for 6 to 36 hours to stabilise the vehicle temperature.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.9.1.title: REESS charge
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.9.1.body: For OVC-HEVs, the REESS shall be fully charged in accordance with the charging requirements described in paragraph 2.2.3. of Appendix 4 to Annex B8 during the soaking described in paragraph 6.6.1.9. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.10.title: Fuel drain and refill
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.10.body: The fuel tank of the vehicle shall be drained and filled up to 40 ±2 per cent of the tank's nominal capacity with reference fuel at a temperature of 18 °C ±2 °C.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.11.title: Soak
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.11.body: The vehicle shall be subsequently parked for a minimum of 6 hours to a maximum of 36 hours in the soak area at 20 °C ±2 °C to stabilise the fuel temperature.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.12.title: Fuel tank depressurisation
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.12.body: The tank pressure shall be subsequently released so as not to abnormally raise the inside pressure of the fuel tank. This may be done by opening the fuel cap of the vehicle. Regardless of the method of depressurisation, the vehicle shall be returned to its original condition within 1 minute. After this action, the vehicle carbon canister shall be connected again.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.13.lb: 6.6.1.13. The procedures in paragraphs 6.5.6. to 6.5.9.8. inclusive of this annex shall b…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.1.13.body: The procedures in paragraphs 6.5.6. to 6.5.9.8. inclusive of this annex shall be followed.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.2.lb: 6.6.2. In the case that the fuel tank relief pressure is lower than 30 kPa
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.2.title: In the case that the fuel tank relief pressure is lower than 30 kPa
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.6.2.body: The test shall be performed as described in paragraphs 6.6.1.1. to 6.6.1.13. inclusive of this annex. However, in this case, the ambient temperature described in paragraph 6.5.9.1. of this annex shall be replaced by the profile specified in Table C3/2 of this annex for the diurnal emission test. [TABLE:REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.TABLE-C3/2]

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.lb: 6.7. Stand-alone test procedure for sealed fuel tank systems
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.title: Stand-alone test procedure for sealed fuel tank systems
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.body: 6.7.1 Measurement of depressurisation puff loss loading mass

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.1.1.lb: 6.7.1.1. The procedures in paragraphs 6.6.1.1. to 6.6.1.7.2. inclusive of this annex sha…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.1.1.body: The procedures in paragraphs 6.6.1.1. to 6.6.1.7.2. inclusive of this annex shall be performed. The depressurisation puff loss loading mass is defined as the difference in weight of the vehicle carbon canister before paragraph 6.6.1.6. of this annex is applied and after paragraph 6.6.1.7.2. of this annex is applied.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.1.2.lb: 6.7.1.2. The depressurisation puff loss overflow from the vehicle carbon canister shall …
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.1.2.body: The depressurisation puff loss overflow from the vehicle carbon canister shall be measured according to paragraphs 6.6.1.8.1. and 6.6.1.8.2. inclusive of this Annex and fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6.6.1.8.3. in this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.lb: 6.7.2. Hot soak and diurnal breathing evaporative emissions test
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.title: Hot soak and diurnal breathing evaporative emissions test

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.1.lb: 6.7.2.1. In the case that the fuel tank relief pressure is greater than or equal to 30 k…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.1.title: In the case that the fuel tank relief pressure is greater than or equal to 30 kPa

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.1.1.lb: 6.7.2.1.1. The test shall be performed as described in paragraphs 6.5.1. to 6.5.3. and
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.1.1.title: The test shall be performed as described in paragraphs 6.5.1. to 6.5.3. and

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.1.2.lb: 6.7.2.1.2. The carbon canister shall be aged according to the sequence described in paragr…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.1.2.body: The carbon canister shall be aged according to the sequence described in paragraph 5.1. to 5.1.3.1.3. inclusive of this annex and shall be loaded and purged according to paragraph 6.6.1.5. of this annex.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.1.3.lb: 6.7.2.1.3. The aged carbon canister shall subsequently be loaded according to the procedur…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.1.3.body: The aged carbon canister shall subsequently be loaded according to the procedure described in paragraph 6.5.5.4. However, instead of loading to breakthrough as described in paragraph 6.5.5.4.4., the total loading mass shall be determined in accordance with paragraph 6.7.1.1. of this annex. At the request of the manufacturer, the reference fuel may alternatively be used instead of butane. The carbon canister shall be disconnected.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.1.4.lb: 6.7.2.1.4. The procedures in paragraphs 6.6.1.10. to 6.6.1.13. inclusive of this annex sha…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.1.4.body: The procedures in paragraphs 6.6.1.10. to 6.6.1.13. inclusive of this annex shall be followed.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.2.lb: 6.7.2.2. In the case that the fuel tank relief pressure is lower than 30 kPa
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.2.title: In the case that the fuel tank relief pressure is lower than 30 kPa
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.6.7.2.2.body: The test shall be performed as described in paragraphs 6.7.2.1.1. to 6.7.2.1.4. inclusive of this annex. However, in this case, the ambient temperature described in paragraph 6.5.9.1. of this annex shall be modified in accordance with the profile specified in Table A1/1 of this annex for the diurnal emission test.

REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.7.1.lb: 7.1. The evaporative emission tests described in paragraphs 6. to 6.7.2.2. inclusive…
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.7.1.body: The evaporative emission tests described in paragraphs 6. to 6.7.2.2. inclusive of this annex allow the hydrocarbon emissions from the puff loss overflow, diurnal and hot soak tests to be calculated. Evaporative losses from each of these tests shall be calculated using the initial and final hydrocarbon concentrations, temperatures and pressures in the enclosure, together with the net enclosure volume. The following equation shall be used: [EQ:REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.7.1.EQ-1] CHC is the measured hydrocarbon concentration in the enclosure, ppm volume in C1 equivalent; V is the net enclosure volume corrected for the volume of the vehicle with the windows and the luggage compartment open, m . If the volume of the vehicle is not known, a volume of 1.42 m shall be subtracted; T is the ambient chamber temperature, K; P is the barometric pressure, kPa; H/C is the hydrogen to carbon ratio where: H/C is taken to be 2.33 for puff loss overflow measurement in SHED and diurnal test losses; H/C is taken to be 2.20 for hot soak losses; H/C is taken to be 2.67 for calibration; k is 1.2 × 10^-4 × (12 + H/C), (g × K/(m3 × kPa)); i is the initial reading; f is the final reading;
REG154.04.ANNEX-C1.APP3.7.1.foot: Distinguishing number of the country which has granted/extended/refused/withdrawn approval (see approval provisions in the regulation).
